label: copy phase: input f (echoed), strongest when next output is n, mid-sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and 93% of activations (95% of mass) fall on steps where the input is the echoed token f; the remaining 5% are on input n. It never fires in the original or delimiter phase, or on the first occurrence of a token. Only about 4.5% of copy-phase f inputs activate it, so it is a sparse sub-feature of input f. What drives magnitude: the next output being n (f followed by n in the original sequence; the top activations are all ...f n... with f at original position 2, peaking at recall_idx 3 with 4-5 outputs still to go). Next output f is second (9x lift). Activations are weak at early recall positions (0-1, none) and at the last outputs. Input f with output n, recall_idx >= 3 and to_go >= 2 has precision 0.90 but covers only 18% of activations. The rest are low-magnitude f inputs spread across many next outputs, and no simple condition captures them.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: f, n, -, u, e, v; least: 0, <DEL>, a, m) and the token being output (most: n, f, u, s, a, w; least: 2, m, -, 3); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=7 & t=10, t=11.
